scope.description: In-process single-voter cluster at protocol version 3 with 50ms timeouts and RestoreCommittedLogs enabled: bootstrap, become leader, commit five commands, restart on the same InmemCommitTrackingStore/InmemStore/InmemSnapshotStore with the flag so the configuration is empty (recorded: zero servers, no leader within two seconds, staged commit 6, log last index 7), then attempt live bootstrap on the running node and, after stopping it, RecoverCluster with the original configuration followed by a fresh NewRaft; each step records the outcome and the resulting configuration size.
assumptions: Live bootstrap and RecoverCluster are the two operator entry points the library documents for (re)establishing a configuration; both are called with the configuration this cluster was originally bootstrapped with.
RecoverCluster is documented as an explicit, unsafe-by-design disaster-recovery operation, so its success here is a repair capability, not a normal path.
The stores are the real ones produced by the earlier phases; nothing is fabricated.
excluded: No multi-voter scenario: the probe asks whether an operator can repair one node's configuration, which the failing cluster-wide state needs before any election is possible.

basis.prefix: Real bootstrap, real election, real commits, real graceful shutdown and restart with the flag reproducing the empty configuration, then the two operator entry points called through the public API with the same stores and configuration.

comparisons.description: Live bootstrap on a node whose state exists must either repair the configuration or, if it refuses, leave the state unchanged; the assertion records whether it repaired it.
The documented disaster-recovery path must restore the supplied configuration on the stopped node, so that the node can lead again.
